title: A group exact between two finite groups is finite
statement: Let $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ be homomorphisms of abelian groups which are exact at $B$, i.e. $\ker g=\operatorname{im}f$. If $A$ and $C$ are finite, then $B$ is finite. (Indeed $\operatorname{im}f$ is a quotient of the finite $A$ and $B/\operatorname{im}f=B/\ker g\cong\operatorname{im}g$ is a subgroup of the finite $C$, so $B$, an extension of two finite groups, is finite.)
